doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Blue Note years with New Orleans musicians
summary: He played for years with Vidacovich and Singleton or Huntington and enjoyed the New Orleans feel.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: You did “Middle Class White Boy,” which became a very popular number for you, I think. Then, when that label ended, you did a number of recordings for Blue Note subsequently, one of them with a bunch of New Orleans musicians, like John Vidacovich and Tony Dagradi, up until 1997, with Gimcracks and Geegaws. Anything to say about that period?

Well, I played with John Vidacovich all the time, and Jim Singleton, I think....no, Bill Huntington was on the bass. I played with both of those guys for years. I got the guys that they worked with on the Blues Alley... No, it was...
You mean, where you played there...
But you played with those guys for so long, it sounds like they were giving you a feel you were looking for, a Gulf Coast thing...
Well, I didn’t think about that. I just knew them both, and I knew what they could do.

I think it sounded like you had fun with them all the time. Every time you played with different sections...they were distinctive, and it seemed like... I just remember, it seemed like you had fun playing with Vidacovich and Singleton.
It had the New Orleans feel to it.
Yeah. It was always high energy. It seemed like they were that kind of band.
